summary: Rio Arriba County, NM lookout on the Jicarilla Reservation: a 60-ft steel tower put up in June 1932, registered 1999 and listed as standing; BIA-administered, no public access described.

access.note: Located on the Jicarilla Reservation and administered by the Bureau of Indian Affairs. The sources read describe no public access; ask the tribal government before visiting.

events.note: First used as a lookout point, per the register
60' steel tower with 7' x 7' cab erected in June 1932 at a reported cost of $92
Staffed by a lookout-fireman the year after the tower went up (first staffing the register records)

notes_for_editor: Two sources only. Standing status rests on the FFLA New Mexico list; the register does not state current condition. The register's height figure is 60 feet, converted to 18.3 m for height_m; it may be the tower height rather than cab floor height. Record coordinates (36.867458, -107.06948) sit about 50 m from the FFLA point (36.86785, -107.06985); not treated as an error. Record design and height were null and are now filled from the register. Access is a judgment from the reservation location and the BIA administrator field; no visitor information was found. Used 2 WebSearch calls and 2 page reads (NHLR, FFLA list).
